take_homes: Putting my context in a file the agent reads each session beats better prompts. My team of fourteen could share one.
Name a framework, tune it, and let the agent run it. Be specific about what I hate or want, because vague input gives the average answer.
The agent flatters its own work. Use a cold, second reader and my own judgment before I trust a self-review.

monday.move: Write a one-page context file for the usage-pricing decision: sources, which sources I distrust, and what generic looks like. Fill in prework/module-2-start.md. Then run the pilot-cohort brief against it and get a cold read.
monday.who: Me, then the pricing working group
monday.when: Monday morning, before the Module 2 session
monday.stop_condition: If the cold read finds the brief still generic after one added detail, I stop and rethink the context

misconception.why: It says the model didn't improve and the context did, and the file idea points the same way. I now see context and a reusable file as the lever. I'm not sure prompts don't matter, and I haven't tried it on my own work yet.

one_line: Useful idea about context files and a cold second read, but I spent most of the hour on a personal website and only the last page touched my real work.
